events.title: Andrew Tanenbaum creates MINIX
events.summary: Andrew Tanenbaum created MINIX in 1987 — a teaching microkernel OS that inspired Linus Torvalds to build Linux.
events.about: Tanenbaum's textbooks and MINIX shaped OS education worldwide. The famous Tanenbaum–Torvalds microkernel debate defined architectural trade-offs developers still argue about.

narrative.whyChosen: MINIX was the direct inspiration for Linux's initial design.
narrative.whyImportant: It made operating system source code accessible to students.
narrative.problemSolved: Unix source was proprietary and unavailable for classroom study.
